messages:
devon: Snyk just flagged netty 4.1.x for a deserialization reachability issue (CVE-2026-XXXXX). scan shows 'reachable via server pipeline' but our shape is worker-only. tagging eng-runtime + ops for triage. https://snyk.io/vuln/CVE-2026-XXXXX
maria-security: can you paste the exact dependency line and where netty is used?
devon: sure — it's pulled in by fast-net-connector: 
```
fast-net-connector==2.3.1
- netty-all==4.1.72.Final
```
We only instantiate an outbound client in the ingestion worker (no public endpoints).
ton y-eng-runtime: quick note: we use netty for internal RPC to the model pool. not exposed to internet. still want to be careful with deserialization APIs.
aaron-ml: we don't accept arbitrary payloads; RPC proto is strict and validated.
sarah-ops: are there any WAF / LB rules that could block exploit patterns? we could add a rule for the next window.
maria-security: CVSS listed by Snyk is 7.5 based on remote exploitation. but their repro steps assume server-side handler deserializes user-supplied java objects. need to confirm if our code ever calls ObjectInputStream on untrusted data.
devon: grep shows only protobuf parsing on the wire. no ObjectInputStream usage in repo.
maria-security: ok that's a strong FP indicator. two paths: 1) mark as FP with short-lived exception while we schedule an upgrade, or 2) apply compensating controls + audit logging and treat as accepted risk until patch. preferences?
ton y-eng-runtime: upgrade path: netty 4.1.73 has a patch, but requires rebuild of fast-net-connector and running integration against model pool. estimate 1 sprint.
sarah-ops: we can push a temporary WAF rule to block serialized-java payloads at the LB edge. also enable extra audit logging on the worker ingress for the next 30 days.
maria-security: would like legal signoff if we take risk acceptance route. @judy-legal can you weigh in on formal exception window length?
judy-legal: for infra-level findings where exposure is limited and we've got mitigations, we prefer a 14-day window with required mitigations in place (WAF + audit) and a remediation ticket assigned with owner. also require a short post-mortem if anything odd appears.
sec-bot: [automated] New exception request created: EXC-2026-0143, owner: @devon, due_date: 2026-04-12
maria-security: Devon, please attach minimal repro attempt result and a link to dependency upgrade PR when created. we'll approve provisional exception once mitigations are live.
devon: created ticket INC-4671 to add WAF rule + audit logging. PR for upgrade branch: https://git.internal/fast-net-connector/pull/289 (WIP).
sarah-ops: deployed WAF rule in edge-canary. monitoring alert set on suspicious content-type and protobuf parsing errors.
ton y-eng-runtime: added runtime guard: reject any request with header X-Serialized-Java present. quick patch deployed behind feature flag.
maria-security: I reviewed the grep output and integration tests — looks like false positive for deserialization. provisioning provisional approval for 14 days with required mitigations: WAF rule, ingress audit logs, runtime guard, and upgrade PR by EOW.
judy-legal: noted. I'll log the compliance note.
devon: thanks. plan: finish PR + CI, then schedule upgrade deploy to canary, then to prod. timeline ~10 days.
sec-bot: [automated] Exception EXC-2026-0143 status=provisionally_approved until 2026-04-12 by @maria-security
deploy-bot: canary deploy for fast-net-connector v2.4.0-upgrade scheduled for 2026-04-02 03:00 UTC
aaron-ml: leaving note: model-serving clients will be pinged for compatibility but protobuf schema unchanged.
maria-security: final ask — add a short eval harness that fuzzes the ingress and confirm no unsafe deserialization paths. tag me when ready.
devon: will add harness to INC-4671 and link results. thanks team :thumbsup:
